item.title: In 2022, conservators X-raying a Van Gogh painting in Edinburgh found a hidden self-portrait of the artist on the back of the canvas, concealed for more than a century under layers of glue and cardboard
item.description: A self-portrait of Vincent van Gogh was discovered concealed behind another painting after many years. The hidden portrait was found during routine examinations ahead of an exhibition. This discovery highlights Van Gogh's habit of reusing canvases due to financial difficulties throughout his life. Conservators are now working to reveal the portrait without damaging the original painting. Visitors to the exhibition were able to view the hidden portrait's X-ray image.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Texas man Christophe Waggoner began October's Child in 2017; has gifted 8,000 Halloween costumes to families and plans to give away 4,000 in 2026
item.description: Christophe Waggoner established a charity called October's Child to provide Halloween costumes for children. He began the initiative after recalling his own childhood experiences with costumes. Over the years, the charity has grown significantly, distributing nearly 8,000 costumes to families in need. In the upcoming event, he plans to give away over 4,000 costumes for various age groups. Waggoner's efforts illustrate the positive impact of community support on childhood celebrations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Inside Bieber Couple's Condo: Justin and Hailey add $12m West Village home; waterfront NYC base
item.description: Justin and Hailey Bieber have acquired a $12 million condominium in Manhattan's West Village. This residence features expansive river views and distinct architectural design. The apartment includes four bedrooms and significant amenities for privacy and convenience. The property reflects a modernist style and includes shared amenities like a swimming pool. This purchase adds to the couple's diverse real estate portfolio that spans multiple locations.
item.dc:creator: Khushi

item.title: After 20-Year Search, California Community Buys Cupertino Property for $16.5 Million
item.description: After an extensive search, the West Valley Muslim Association has successfully acquired a property in Cupertino for $16.5 million. This new facility will serve as a permanent home for the community, offering a venue for daily prayers, educational activities, and community gatherings. Supported by a dedicated fundraising campaign, this purchase reflects the growing needs of the local Muslim population, establishing a vital center for faith and fellowship.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 3,700-year-old man buried with stone in his mouth beneath a hearth may have been part of magical ritual
item.description: Approximately 3,700 years ago, a man in southeastern Spain underwent a burial unlike any other. Researchers suggest that this ritual may have been intended to symbolically overcome a threat rather than inflict punishment. The discovery of his body underneath a hearth, with a stone in his mouth, implies an effort to silence him.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: How UKHarvest turned food waste into 10 million meals
item.description: In 2017, Yvonne Thomson founded UKHarvest to address food waste and assist individuals facing food insecurity. Initially starting with one van, the charity has impressively salvaged 10 million meals throughout its journey. Its initiatives, including Community Food Hubs and Grub Clubs, offer not only affordable food but also valuable education. Collecting about 10 tonnes of excess food weekly, UKHarvest enjoys the patronage of Queen Camilla, amplifying its community impact.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Antipodes Island Sees Ground Beetle Numbers Surge 40-Fold After Mice Eradication
item.description: The successful removal of invasive house mice from Antipodes Island has spurred a remarkable resurgence in ground beetle populations, which have increased to around 40 times their former numbers. This ecological transformation highlights the beneficial effects of eradicating invasive species, fostering a healthier food web and aiding in the survival of native bird species. Long-term observation is crucial for comprehending the recovery dynamics of island ecosystems.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Texas’s Historic Imperial Sugar Char House Gets $15M Rescue After 20 Years Vacant
item.description: Sugar Land City Council has given a green light for a $15 million initiative to safeguard the iconic Imperial Sugar Char House. This undertaking aims to stabilize the structure and prevent further deterioration over the years ahead. Work is set to commence shortly, with an anticipated completion by 2028. Officials are still finalizing plans for potential future utilizations, leaving residents eager for tangible development on this cherished landmark.

item.title: Taking antibiotics? Eating a lot of sugar at the same time may make the damage to your gut worse, scientists have found, suggesting that what you eat during a course of antibiotics could affect how well your body recovers
item.description: Research findings indicate that a diet high in sugar can significantly affect the diversity of gut bacteria in patients undergoing antibiotic therapy. The study monitored the food intake and gut microbiome of hospitalized cancer patients treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, revealing a strong connection between elevated sugar levels and shifts in gut bacteria.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: In 1987, an amateur fossil hunter found a T. rex in South Dakota; the $31.8 million skeleton now stands in Abu Dhabi
item.description: In 1987, Stan Sacrison found a T. rex skeleton in South Dakota, which was later sold for $31.8 million. Initially misidentified, the bones were correctly recognized as belonging to a T. rex in 1992. After years at the Black Hills Institute, the skeleton was auctioned and purchased for a museum in Abu Dhabi. Stan is now displayed in a dramatic scene depicting conflicts with another T. rex.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Texas Jury Finds No Legal or Informal Adoption in $1 Million Inheritance Dispute
item.description: In a complex Texas inheritance case, a stepson referred to as 'my child' in a will navigated a treacherous dispute following his father's passing. Despite his claims of informal adoption, the family remained unconvinced. Ultimately, the jury affirmed that no formal or informal adoption occurred. This outcome highlights the necessity of clear legal documentation in estate planning to avoid misunderstandings, particularly within blended families concerning rights to inheritance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Steven Spielberg pulls $29.9 M LA ranch off the market
item.description: Filmmaker Steven Spielberg listed his Los Angeles ranch for $29.9 million but has now taken it off the market. He and his wife purchased the property in 1999 for $5.75 million, intending to create equestrian facilities. After facing opposition from local residents, their renovation plans were significantly reduced over the years. The ranch, known as Dogwood, features a main house with numerous upscale amenities and a 20,000-square-foot riding arena.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: In 1600, William Gilbert called Earth a giant magnet; his book sold for Rs 58.5 lakh in 2026
item.description: William Gilbert's pivotal publication, De Magnete, emerged in 1600, marking a significant shift in the exploration of magnetism and electricity. It introduced key terms and experimental approaches that influenced future electrical studies. The concept of Earth as a colossal magnet was groundbreaking. Recently, a first edition fetched $61,440 at a Christie’s auction, highlighting its enduring significance and the continued fascination it holds in scientific discourse.
